sim2real logo · round 2 · 40 proposals

2026-10-28 · 20 gear logos (G) and 20 s2r type logos (S) · digital vs real · a logo first; the icon gets simplified from the pick later

Gear: recommend G01 Split Gear, then G02 Screen Hub and G03 Half Screen (take G03 if the screen has to be in the logo). Type: recommend S01 2 Boundary, then S02 Res Ramp and S03 s2r Tiles.

Digital is hard square pixels on a dark screen; real is a machined metal part or set ink type. Pick any number in either section (★), comment, then Copy my picks and paste the text into chat. Round 1's toolbar icon stays Clank's default until a logo is picked and simplified.

Gear logos #2 · score 91

s2r type logos #1 · score 88

S01 2 Boundary

His 'half a computer screen, half in reality' done with the letters: the 2's diagonal is the edge of the screen, a pixel s inside it and a steel r outside it. The 2 itself is the boundary.

s2r type logos #2 · score 87

S02 Res Ramp

The plainest version of 'fades from pixel to real': a coarse pixel s, a finer pixel 2, a set r. Pixel letters are BAM's own block type, so it fits the family.

s2r type logos #3 · score 87

S03 s2r Tiles

The BAM lockup's own form (the B-A-M tiles) applied to s-2-r: a screen tile, an ink tile, a steel tile. The easiest of the type marks to turn into a 24 px icon.

Notes

How they are built

  • One gear, ten teeth, in every logo. Digital = the gear rasterised onto its own square grid, shaded like pixel art (a lit top-left edge, a dark bottom-right edge). Real = the same outline as a machined part: a steel gradient, a rim, a recessed web with lathe rings, a hub and a bore.
  • Source in brand/logos/round2/: geom.py (gear, pixels, metal, screens), logos.py (the 20), scores.py, wordmark.py. Each logo is drawn twice, for light and for dark grounds.
  • The s2r set uses Ubuntu Sans 800; its pixel letters are those same outlines rasterised onto a square grid, so the pixel s and the set s are one letter at two resolutions.
  • Every logo was rendered headlessly at 240 px and 32 px, on light and dark, and looked at. Redrawn after looking: gear Pixel Shadow (a floor shadow read as a slab), Loupe (the lens showed a green blob, not teeth), Sim Floor (a light floor vanished at 32 px); type Stencil r (its shadow showed through the cut), Screen Escape (crowded), Mirror Line (the reflection was too heavy).

Palette

  • BAM Grid Purist: ink #0E100E, paper #FBFBF8, BAM Green #2F6F4F, lit on dark as #35DE95; steel greys for the real gear.
  • Palette breaks on purpose, marked on their cards: G Circuit Cast and S Circuit s (bronze casting, PCB pads), S Subpixel (real RGB stripes). G Sim Floor keeps its floor dark on both grounds, as a sim viewport does.

Wordmark and files

  • 'sim' in square pixels (BAM's block letters), '2real' in Ubuntu Sans Bold: the word itself goes from digital to real. The same wordmark is used in all 20 lockups.
  • Per logo, gear set in brand/logos/round2/ and type set in brand/logos/round2/s2r/: NN-slug.svg, -dark.svg, -lockup.svg, -lockup-dark.svg, preview32/NN-slug-32.png.
  • For the type logos the lockup repeats the word (s2r + sim2real), as a monogram beside its full name does; use the bare mark where that is too much.
